examples.en: I was checked for a fever at the airport quarantine station.

examples.ko: 외국에서 과일을 가져오면 검역소를 거쳐야 해요.
examples.en: If you bring fruit from abroad, it has to go through quarantine.
I heard a new quarantine station opened near the port.

examples.ko: 강아지를 데리고 입국해서 검역소로 먼저 갔어요.
examples.en: I entered the country with my puppy and went to the quarantine office first.
The quarantine station was crowded with people from early morning.

examples.ko: 검역소의 안내에 따라 줄을 서 주세요.
examples.en: Please line up following the quarantine station's instructions.

explain: 주로 공항이나 항구에서 사람뿐 아니라 동물, 식물, 음식물을 확인하는 곳으로 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 일에 대해서는 '검역'이라고 하고, 곳은 '검역소'라고 해요.
explain_en: It often appears in the news as a place at airports or ports that checks not only people but also animals, plants and food. The procedure itself is '검역', and the place is '검역소'.

examples.ko: 수도 계량기를 보고 이번 달 물 사용량을 확인했어요.
examples.en: I checked this month's water usage by looking at the water meter.
The gas meter is on the balcony.
The numbers on the meter suddenly went up a lot.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 수도 계량기가 얼지 않게 덮어 둬야 해요.
examples.en: In winter you have to cover the water meter so it doesn't freeze.
The meter is making a strange noise.

examples.ko: 전기 계량기 교체 때문에 잠깐 정전돼요.
examples.en: The power will go out briefly because the electric meter is being replaced.

explain: 집집마다 달려 있어서 '계량기를 확인하다', '계량기가 돌아가다', '계량기가 얼다'처럼 써요. 수도·가스·전기 앞에 종류를 붙여 말하고, 숫자를 읽으러 오는 일은 '검침'이라고 해요. 요리용 '계량컵', '계량스푼'의 '계량'과 같은 말이에요.
explain_en: Every home has one, and it is used as '계량기를 확인하다', '계량기가 돌아가다' and '계량기가 얼다'. Put the type in front, such as water, gas or electric; the visit to read the numbers is called '검침'. The '계량' is the same as in the cooking tools '계량컵' and '계량스푼'.

examples.en: Could you give me the check, please?
I think the bill came out wrong.
A service charge is added to the bill.
I will take the bill.
Keep the bill too, just like a receipt.
The amount on the bill was less than I expected.

explain: 식당에서 '계산서 주세요'라고 해도 되고 '계산해 주세요'라고 해도 돼요. 영수증은 돈을 낸 뒤에 받는 종이, 계산서는 낼 돈이 적힌 종이로 나눠 생각하면 돼요.
explain_en: At a restaurant you can say either '계산서 주세요' or '계산해 주세요'. Think of a 영수증 (receipt) as the paper you get after paying, and a 계산서 as the paper listing what you owe.

examples.en: I lost my key, so I called the management office.

examples.ko: 아파트 관리소는 평일 아홉 시에 열어요.
examples.en: The apartment management office opens at nine on weekdays.
The management office put up a notice.

examples.ko: 이사하기 전에 관리소에 미리 알려야 해요.
examples.en: You need to tell the management office in advance before moving.

examples.ko: 관리소 직원이 고장 난 엘리베이터를 고쳐 줬어요.
examples.en: A management office staff member fixed the broken elevator.

examples.ko: 관리소로 가면 택배를 찾을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go to the management office, you can pick up your package.

explain: 주로 아파트나 건물을 관리하는 사무실을 말해요. 아파트에서는 '관리사무소'나 '관리실'이라고도 해요. 이웃 소음, 주차, 고장 같은 일을 문의할 때 가는 곳이에요.
explain_en: It mostly means the office that manages an apartment complex or building. In apartments it is also called '관리사무소' or '관리실'. It is where you go to ask about neighbor noise, parking or repairs.

examples.en: The management office takes noise complaints in the apartment complex.

examples.ko: 형광등 교체는 관리실에 요청하면 해 줘요.
examples.en: If you ask the management office, they will replace the light tube.
I asked the man at the management office for the key.
Until what time is the management office open?
The elevator broke down, so I called the management office.

examples.ko: 관리실은 일 층 현관 옆에 있어요.
examples.en: The management office is on the first floor next to the entrance.

explain: 아파트나 건물을 관리하는 사무실이에요. 정식 이름은 '관리사무소'이고, 입구를 지키는 '경비실'과는 달라요.
explain_en: It is the office that looks after an apartment complex or building. The formal name is '관리사무소', and it differs from the '경비실' (guard booth) at the entrance.

examples.en: I applied polish to my shoes and wiped them.
This polish doesn't smell strong.
Thanks to the polish, the floor sparkles.

examples.ko: 광택제가 다 떨어져서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: The polish ran out, so I have to buy more.
Try rubbing small scratches with polish.
Even without polish, a dry towel is enough.

explain: 물건 표면을 반짝이게 하려고 바르는 약품이에요. 구두, 자동차, 가구에 쓰는 종류가 달라서 보통 '구두 광택제'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여요. 이 약품으로 닦는 행동은 '광내다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is a product applied to make a surface shine. Different kinds exist for shoes, cars and furniture, so people usually put the object before it, as in '구두 광택제'. The action of polishing with it is '광내다'.

examples.en: I got my room key at the hotel front desk.
I asked the information desk staff for directions.
The desk editor revises the article the reporter wrote.

examples.ko: 데스크에 맡겨 두시면 제가 나중에 찾아갈게요.
examples.en: If you leave it at the desk, I'll pick it up later.

examples.ko: 병원 데스크 앞에서 접수 순서를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I waited my turn to register in front of the hospital desk.

examples.ko: 이 기사는 데스크의 허락이 있어야 나갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: This article can run only with the desk editor's approval.

explain: 책상은 '책상'이라고 하고, 데스크는 호텔·병원·회사의 안내 창구나 신문사의 편집 책임자를 말할 때 써요. '프런트'도 호텔 안내 창구를 가리켜서 거의 같은 상황에 쓰여요. 사무실 책상을 데스크라고 하는 일은 드물어요.
explain_en: A study table is 책상; 데스크 is used for a reception counter at a hotel, hospital, or office, or for the editor in charge at a newspaper. 프런트 is also used for a hotel front desk in nearly the same situations. Calling an office table a 데스크 is rare.

examples.en: If there's something you don't know, click Help.

examples.ko: 선생님이 짧은 도움말을 한마디 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher gave me a short word of advice.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 도움말이 한국어로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This program's help section is in Korean.

examples.ko: 그분의 도움말 덕분에 문제를 쉽게 풀었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to that person's tip, I solved the problem easily.
If you need any advice, just tell me anytime.

examples.ko: 면접 준비에 도움말을 주실 분 계세요?
examples.en: Is there anyone who can give me some tips for interview prep?

explain: '조언'보다 가볍고 짧게, 도움이 되는 말을 해 줄 때 써요. 컴퓨터 프로그램의 '도움말(Help)' 메뉴도 같은 말이에요. 비슷한 말로 '힌트'도 있지만 '도움말'은 문제 풀이뿐 아니라 일상 조언에도 써요.
explain_en: It is lighter and shorter than '조언' (advice) and is used when someone says something helpful. The 'Help' menu in computer programs is also called '도움말'. A similar word is '힌트' (hint), but '도움말' also covers everyday advice, not just solving problems.

examples.en: The landlord pressed me to pay the rent.
The company keeps urging us to hand in the report quickly.
If you keep pushing, I end up not wanting to work.

examples.ko: 도서관에서 책을 반납하라고 독촉하는 문자가 왔어요.
examples.en: I got a text from the library urging me to return the book.
Please don't nag your child to do the homework.
It's hard to press my friend about the money I lent.

explain: 돈, 서류, 기한처럼 해야 할 일을 빨리 하라고 계속 재촉할 때 써요. '재촉하다'가 더 넓게 쓰이고, '독촉하다'는 갚아야 할 돈이나 내야 할 것에 특히 자주 나와요. '독촉장', '독촉 전화'처럼 명사로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when you keep pressing someone to do something they owe, such as money, documents or deadlines. '재촉하다' has a broader range, while '독촉하다' appears especially often with money to be repaid or things to be handed in. It also works as a noun, as in '독촉장' and '독촉 전화'.

examples.en: The district office issues residence certificates.
The bank issued a new card.
The school will issue a graduation certificate.

examples.ko: 서류를 발급하는 창구는 이 층에 있어요.
examples.en: The counter that issues documents is on the second floor.

examples.ko: 직원이 증명서를 발급하고 나서 제게 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: After the staff issued the certificate, they explained it to me.
The staff issued a receipt and gave it to me.

explain: 발급하다는 주는 쪽인 구청, 은행, 학교가 주어예요. 받는 쪽은 '발급받다'를 써요. 그래서 '구청이 여권을 발급했어요'와 '여권을 발급받았어요'가 둘 다 맞아요.
explain_en: The subject of 발급하다 is the issuing side, such as a district office, bank or school. The receiving side uses '발급받다', so both '구청이 여권을 발급했어요' and '여권을 발급받았어요' are correct.

examples.en: You must drive slowly in front of a school.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 터널 안에서 서행하는 차가 많아요.
examples.en: On rainy days, many cars slow down inside the tunnel.

examples.ko: 이 구간은 공사 때문에 서행 운전을 해야 해요.
examples.en: This section is under construction, so you have to drive slowly.
There was an accident, so we kept crawling along the highway.

examples.ko: 앞차가 서행해서 약속에 늦을 것 같아요.
examples.en: The car ahead is going slowly, so I think I'll be late for my appointment.
The road sign says 'slow down'.

explain: '천천히 가다'와 같은 뜻이지만 서행은 주로 운전이나 교통 안내에서 써요. 보통 '서행하다'나 '서행 운전'의 형태로 말하고, 반대로 규정 속도를 넘는 것은 '과속'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means going slowly like '천천히 가다', but 서행 is used mainly for driving and traffic notices. It usually appears as '서행하다' or '서행 운전', and the opposite, exceeding the speed limit, is '과속'.

examples.ko: 선생님이 문제 푸는 방법을 자상히 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher kindly explained how to solve the problem.

examples.ko: 할머니는 제 이야기를 늘 자상히 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Grandma always listens to my stories with care.

examples.ko: 길을 모른다고 하니까 직원이 자상히 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: When I said I didn't know the way, the staff member explained it patiently.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 약 먹는 법을 자상히 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: The doctor carefully told me how to take the medicine.

examples.ko: 어머니가 편지에 안부를 자상히 적어 보내셨어요.
examples.en: My mother wrote about how she was doing in detail and sent the letter.

examples.ko: 모르는 부분은 제가 자상히 가르쳐 드릴게요.
examples.en: I will teach you the parts you don't know, step by step.

explain: '자세히'가 더 일상적이고 내용이 꼼꼼하다는 느낌이에요. '자상히'는 상대를 배려하며 친절하게 해 주는 태도가 같이 느껴져요. 주로 '자상히 알려 주다, 설명해 주다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '자세히' is the more common word and stresses thoroughness. '자상히' also carries a caring, kind attitude toward the listener. It often appears as '자상히 알려 주다' or '자상히 설명해 주다'.

en: full to the brim; a whole load of

examples.en: I filled the basket full of strawberries.

examples.ko: 가방 한가득 책을 넣고 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to school with my bag full of books.

examples.ko: 아이가 입 한가득 밥을 넣고 웃었어요.
examples.en: The child smiled with a mouthful of rice.
Tears filled up in her eyes.

examples.ko: 시장에서 두 손 한가득 채소를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought two handfuls of vegetables at the market.
Laughter spread all through the room.

explain: '가득'과 거의 같은 뜻인데 '한'이 붙어 더 푸짐하고 넉넉한 느낌이 나요. '딸기 한가득', '마음 한가득'처럼 명사 뒤에 쓰기도 하고, '한가득 담다'처럼 동사 앞에도 써요. 대화에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '가득', but the '한' adds a fuller, more generous feel. It can follow a noun, as in '딸기 한가득' and '마음 한가득', or come before a verb, as in '한가득 담다'. It is common in conversation.
